content.text:
Yes—Twyne already has Standard.site publishing, but not full “publish to any domain” support.

- Twyne-hosted publishing creates public pages at `twyne.love/{handle}/{slug}` through **File → Share → Publish now**. These can be updated or unpublished. See [folio-menu.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/folio/folio-menu.tsx:640).
- Bluesky/PDS publishing is also present under **File → Share → Publish to your PDS**. It creates `site.standard.publication` and `site.standard.document` records containing the article’s Markdown and text in the writer’s own ATProto repository. See [standard-site.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/standard-site.ts:1).

What it does not currently have:

- Per-writer custom domains
- Publishing directly to WordPress, Ghost, Medium, Substack, or arbitrary websites
- Generic Micropub/webhook publishing destinations

Also, the Standard.site implementation isn’t fully finished. [Standard.site’s verification contract](https://standard.site/docs/quick-start) requires a `/.well-known/site.standard.publication` response and a document `<link>` pointing back to the AT record. Twyne doesn’t currently provide those correctly. Its PDS records also claim a `/p/{folioId}` page, while Twyne’s actual reader uses `/{handle}/{slug}` ([reader route](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/[handle]/[slug]/index.tsx:1)).

So the honest verdict is: **yes to Twyne pages and Standard.site records; no to real custom-domain or multi-platform publishing yet.** Standard.site itself is an interoperable ATProto schema, not a host that automatically deploys the article onto every website. ([Standard.site introduction](https://standard.site/docs/introduction/))
